2010_009_090710regmtg.paragraph: The Troy School District Board of Education's regular meeting agenda and board packet for Tuesday, September 7, 2010, convening at 7:00 PM in the Services Building, 4420 Livernois, Troy, Michigan, covers recognitions, personnel, curriculum reports, and four business items. Three purchases were placed before the Board for action: music instruments totaling $64,087.00 across five vendors, secondary science supplies totaling $41,078.78, and 44 Apple iPads from Apple, Inc. for $24,158.47 through REMC Contract number 155575. The packet also reports general education enrollment of 5,078 students as of September 7, 2010, and carries the approved minutes of the August 17, 2010 workshop and board meeting.

Meeting
Troy School District Board of Education Regular Meeting, Tuesday, September 7, 2010, 7:00 PM, Services Building, 4420 Livernois, Troy, MI 48098. District offices at 4400 Livernois, Troy, Michigan 48098, 248.823.4000. Meetings are cablecast on TS-TV Channel 19 (Comcast) and Channel 15 (WOW) every Monday and Wednesday at 2:00 and 9:00 p.m. except July and August.

Recognitions
Mark Martin (Boulan Park Middle School), Melissa Rehbine (Smith Middle School), and Jennifer Slade (Larson Middle School), all mathematics teachers, were named winners of the 2010 Edyth May Sliffe Award for Distinguished Middle School Mathematics Teaching, sponsored by the Mathematical Association of America and tied to the American Junior High School Mathematics Exam. Separately, for the 21st straight year the district earned the Association of School Business Officials International Certificate of Excellence in Financial Reporting, for the Comprehensive Annual Financial Report for the fiscal year ended June 30, 2009; Mark Rajter, Assistant Superintendent for Business Services, was recognized.

Consent agenda: prior minutes
The August 17, 2010 Special Board Workshop ran 5:40 p.m. to 6:50 p.m. with Mike Zinn, Consultant for Facilities Study. The August 17, 2010 regular meeting, called to order at 7:00 p.m. with all seven members present and roughly 35 audience members, recognized 27 all-state athletes and adopted motions 10-081 through 10-092, including the VSC, Inc. infrared wireless microphone bid at $74,641.00 from the 2004 Capital Projects Fund, a sidewalk easement with Satyendra and Indira Basu at 553 Colebrook (parcel 88-20-22-252-036), Schools of Choice under Section 105c, the resignation of Tim McAvoy and appointment of Kerry Birmingham, cancellation of the September 23-24, 2010 Fall Retreat, and a September 28, 2010 special workshop.

Personnel
Probationary contracts recommended for 2010-2011: Anne Costello (.68 FTE Math/Tech, Baker), Garrett Lovas (.7 FTE PE/Health, elementary), Katie Oxendine (1.0 FTE Resource Room, Baker), Nathan Reynolds (.8 FTE English/Science, Smith), Sara Seckel (1.0 FTE MoCI, Athens), Kara Spodarek (1.0 FTE Resource Room, Baker), and Sarah Young (1.0 ASD Classroom, Morse).

Curriculum reports
Bob Stromayer, Director of Continuing Education, reported on 2010 summer learning. Selected enrollments: Troy Sports Camps 1,212; TCC Workshops/Seminars 1,139; High School Summer School 880; GRASP (Books) 768; Drivers Education 557; Learn to Swim 387; Adventure Island 366. The enrollment update lists general education counts of 4937 on June 30, 2010, 4947 on July 9, 2010, 5056 on August 27, 2010, and 5078 on September 7, 2010. Building projections as of September 7, 2010 show Total Elementary 5,171, Total MS 2,835, Total HS 4,088, and TOTAL STUDENTS 12,094, against September 2009 figures of 5,138, 2,811, 4,076, and 12,025.

Business
Mark Rajter and Ken Miller, Director of Operations, reported on summer 2010 bond projects: flooring, artificial turf fields, parking lot gates, tennis courts, door replacement and card readers, sound and curtain panels, lighting upgrades, playground resurfacing at Hill Elementary, and parking lot repaving at ten sites including Central Office, Smith, Wass, Troy Union, Morse, Schroeder, Barnard and Niles.

| Item | Vendor(s) | Amount | Fund |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Music instruments (Bid 9690) | A & G Central Music, Sam Ash Quickship, Shar Products Co., Taylor Music, Washington Music Center | $64,087.00 | 2004 Capital Projects Fund |
| Secondary science supplies (Bid 9686) | Pasco Scientific, Science Kit, Sargent Welch, EAI Education, Vernier Software and others | $41,078.78 | 2010-2011 General Fund and 2004 Capital Projects Fund |
| Apple iPads (REMC) | Apple, Inc. | $24,158.47 | 2004 Capital Projects Fund |

Closed session
A resolution under the Michigan Open Meetings Act, Public Act 267, Section 8(c) was proposed to move into closed session to discuss negotiations, by roll call vote.

Board packet for the Troy School District Board of Education Regular Meeting held Tuesday, September 7, 2010 at 7:00 PM in the Services Building, 4420 Livernois, Troy, MI 48098, with district offices at 4400 Livernois, Troy, Michigan 48098 (248.823.4000). Meetings are cablecast on TS-TV Channel 19 (Comcast) and Channel 15 (WOW) every Monday and Wednesday at 2:00 and 9:00 p.m. except in July and August.

RECOGNITIONS. Item 2.A honors Mark Martin, mathematics teacher at Boulan Park Middle School; Melissa Rehbine, mathematics teacher at Smith Middle School; and Jennifer Slade, mathematics teacher at Larson Middle School, as winners of the 2010 Edyth May Sliffe Award for Distinguished Middle School Mathematics Teaching, sponsored by the Mathematical Association of America and tied to the American Junior High School Mathematics Exam. Item 2.B notes that for the 21st straight year the Troy School District earned the Association of School Business Officials International Certificate of Excellence in Financial Reporting for its Comprehensive Annual Financial Report (CAFR) for the fiscal year ended June 30, 2009; Mark Rajter, Assistant Superintendent for Business Services, and his staff were recognized.

AUGUST 17, 2010 SPECIAL BOARD WORKSHOP MINUTES. President Underwood called the workshop to order at 5:40 p.m. at the Administration Building, with Mrs. Edmunds, Mrs. Fleming, Mr. Hauff, Mr. Miletti, Ms. Philippart, and Mrs. Pochodylo; administrators Dr. Fowler, Mrs. Keeling, Dr. Machesky, Mr. Rajter, and Mr. Witt; and Mike Zinn, Consultant for Facilities Study. Items were Public Communication, Facilities Study, Other, and Adjournment. Adjourned at 6:50 p.m. Submitted by Nancy L. Philippart, Secretary.

AUGUST 17, 2010 BOARD MEETING MINUTES. Called to order at 7:00 p.m. at the Services Building by President Underwood, with Board members Edmunds, Fleming, Hauff, Miletti, Philippart, and Pochodylo; Superintendent Fowler; administrators Bryan, Jolly, Keeling, Machesky, Rajter, and Witt; and approximately 35 additional audience members. The Board recognized 27 high school students named all-state athletes in synchronized swimming, girls track, girls lacrosse, girls water polo, softball, girls soccer and boys track, among them Merna Abdou, Francesca Adamski, Jessica Benton, Skylar Darish, Katie Dunn, Sara Dykowski, Emily Dzik, Samantha Johnson, Lindsey Miller, Emily Raymond, Kristen Soreide, Victoria Troccoli, Jordan Wheatley, Madeline Wideman, James Yau and Carlie Zitkus. A recess was called at 7:10 p.m., reconvening at 7:15 p.m.

Motions, each carried Ayes 7 / Nays 0: 10-081 (Fleming/Philippart), consent agenda items A, B and C, being minutes of the July 13, 2010 meeting, the Treasurer's Report for June and July 2010, and a Bid Award for Diesel Fuel. 10-082 (Hauff/Miletti), personnel recommendations with new hires Kathy Cappuso, Angela DeClerck, Courtney Fix, James Kurecka, Eileen Rabourn, Nanette Renkiewicz, and Jennifer Royston. 10-083 (Miletti/Fleming), resignation of Tim McAvoy, Director of Community Relations, effective August 9, 2010. 10-084 (Edmunds/Hauff), a two-year probationary administrative contract without tenure to Ms. Kerry Birmingham as Director, Community & Media Relations effective August 23, 2010. 10-085 (Philippart/Miletti), a Schools of Choice resolution under Section 105c of the State School Aid Act of 1979 as amended by Public Act 300 of 1996; Dr. Fowler indicated the limitation should apply at the 10th grade because IA East has capacity for ten additional students, with an unlimited number of 9th graders considered, and 10-086 (Edmunds/Fleming) amended and approved the resolution for a limited grade 10 program and an unlimited grade 9 program for non-resident students attending a district in another county contiguous with the Oakland Intermediate School District boundaries. 10-087 (Pochodylo/Fleming), the infrared wireless microphone bid to VSC, Inc. for $74,641.00 from the 2004 Capital Projects Fund. 10-088 (Philippart/Edmunds), authorizing Superintendent Barbara A. Fowler, Ph.D. to execute a sidewalk easement agreement with Satyendra and Indira Basu for property at 553 Colebrook, parcel id number 88-20-22-252-036, City of Troy, County of Oakland. 10-089 (Fleming/Hauff), Board Committee Memberships for 2010-11. 10-090 (Hauff/Miletti), cancelling the September 23-24, 2010 Fall Retreat. 10-091 (Philippart/Pochodylo), scheduling a Special Board Workshop for Tuesday, September 28, 2010 at 6:00 p.m. at the Administrative Center. 10-092 (Fleming/Philippart), closed session for negotiations under the Michigan Open Meetings Act, Public Act 267, Section 8(h), by roll call with Pochodylo, Underwood, Edmunds, Fleming, Hauff, Miletti and Philippart voting Yes. The Board entered closed session at 8:30 p.m., reconvened at 9:24 p.m., and adjourned at 9:25 p.m.

PERSONNEL (Item 6.A). Probationary contracts recommended for the 2010-2011 school year, with biographical sketches dated September 7, 2010: Anne Costello, .68 FTE Math/Tech Teacher at Baker Middle School (B.A. College for Creative Studies 1995, Michigan Provisional Certificate June 2010; Ferndale and Birmingham Public Schools; Royal Oak); Garrett Lovas, .7 FTE Physical Education/Health Teacher at the elementary level (B.A. Wayne State University May 2010; Lamphere Schools and Troy School District student teaching; Warren); Katie Oxendine, 1.0 FTE Resource Room Teacher at Baker Middle School (B.A. Hope College May 2009 in Learning Disabilities; Sterling Heights); Nathan Reynolds, .8 FTE English/Science Teacher at Smith Middle School (B.A. Oakland University May 2008; Troy resident); Sara Seckel, 1.0 FTE MoCI Teacher at Athens, Special Education (B.A. Central Michigan University May 2010 in Cognitive Impairment and Health; Troy resident); Kara Spodarek, 1.0 FTE Resource Room Teacher at Baker Middle School (B.A. Michigan State University May 2008 in Special Education; Academy of Oak Park-Whitcomb; Birmingham); and Sarah Young, 1.0 ASD Classroom Teacher at Morse, Special Education (B.S. University of Michigan August 2006 in Early Childhood Development; Rochester Hills).

SUMMER LEARNING UPDATE (Item 7.A). Presented by Bob Stromayer, Director of Continuing Education, acknowledging Jan Keeling, Assistant Superintendent, Elementary Education, and Rich Machesky, Assistant Superintendent, Secondary Education. Elementary programs were Nature's Art, Adventures in Learning, Jump Start, GRASP, Title I, ESL (K-7), and Summer Sensation Camps. Middle school programs were Academic Adventure Courses, Academic Success Courses, and Adventure Island-Destination Success, noting the 16th year of the Rochester Villas Summer Program and a third year of Adventure Island with an 18% enrollment increase. High school offerings were High School Summer School and High School ESL, with stable overall enrollment, a transportation option between high schools, largest enrollments in Intro to PE, World History I and Health, and a second year of high school ESL. Enrollment summary: Troy Sports Camps 1,212; Rochester Villas Camp 55; Title 1 181; ESL 154; Band Camp 145; Orchestra Camp 80; Adventure Island 366; Secondary ESL 33; Special Education Extended Year 61; Adult ESL 112; College Extension 183; Drivers Education 557; Learn to Swim 387; Preschool (TOTS) 21; Summer School Elementary School 181, Middle School 186, High School 880; GRASP (Books) 768; Summer Sensation Camps 252; TCC Workshops/Seminars 1,139.

BOND PROJECTS UPDATE (Item 8.A). Reported by Mark Rajter and Ken Miller, Director of Operations, on summer 2010 bond work: corridor flooring, media center, artificial turf field, two parking lot gate units off the student lot, lighting upgrades, re-surfacing of the main gym floor, door replacement with a completion date of 09/18/2010, and card readers as part of the door installation project at one site; flooring in 73 classrooms, 16 office spaces and corridors on the first, second and third floors, artificial turf field, three parking lot gates off the student lot plus one for receiving and one service gate to the stadium, tennis courts, and door replacement scheduled for mid September at another; and flooring in 23 classrooms, 8 prep/workroom spaces and 1 teacher lounge across two facilities, sound panel replacement of the 700 and 900 block portable wall, and lighting upgrades in the 600 block locker rooms and rest rooms. At International Academy East, flooring in 9 classrooms and the main entrance corridor plus music room sound and curtain panels; at Hill Elementary, flooring in 23 classrooms, main office and conference rooms and a playground resurfacing project, with safety drop zones at 12 elementary sites tilled and weeded before adding surface material per Consumer Product Safety Commission (CPSC) guidelines. Parking lots were repaved at Central Office, the Services Building, Smith, Wass, Troy Union, Morse, International Academy, Schroeder, Barnard and Niles, with storm drain repairs at Niles. Smaller work included landscaping and drainage improvements, painting, drywall repairs, whiteboard removal for Smart-Board installation, and concrete replacement.

MUSIC INSTRUMENTS (Item 8.B, Bid Award #9690). Per an August 30, 2010 memorandum from Frank E. Lams, Supervisor, Purchasing and Budget (1140 Rankin, Troy, MI 48083, 248-823-4052, fax 248-823-4077) to Mark S. Rajter, bids were opened August 24, 2010 for the International Academy East and all 12 elementary schools; 17 potential bidders were solicited with 12 responding, one a "No Bid." Results were reviewed with Ms. J. Keeling, Mr. J. McCoy, Fine Arts Coordinator, and Mr. G. Wood, Costello Principal. Recommended awards: A & G Central Music $900.00 (I.A.E.), total $900.00; Sam Ash Quickship $5,256.00 (elementary), total $5,256.00; Shar Products Co. $6,336.00 (elementary), total $6,336.00; Taylor Music Inc. $13,451.00 I.A.E. and $12,864.00 elementary, total $26,315.00; Washington Music Center $17,528.00 I.A.E. and $7,752.00 elementary, total $25,280.00. Column totals: I.A.E. $31,879.00, Elementary $32,208.00, Total $64,087.00, as an expenditure of the 2004 Capital Projects Fund. Instruments bid included Yamaha YTS-475 Tenor Sax, Yamaha TBS-52 Baritone Sax, Lewis Kayser cello outfits, Selmer 1430P Bb Bass Clarinet, Fox Bassoon 51, Holton H177 Farkas, YEP-321S Euphonium, Jupiter 4 Valve BBb Tuba, Selmer 120B Oboe, and elementary Gemeinhardt, Bach and Eastman flutes, trumpets, trombones and violins. Other bidders included Midwest Musical Imports, Interstate Music, National Educational Music Co., Northeast Music, Brook Mays Music and Marshall Music Co.; McCourt's Music, Melhart Music Center, Nick Rail Music, Southwest Strings and Universal Melody Services gave no response and Suzuki submitted no bid.

SECONDARY SCIENCE SUPPLIES (Item 8.C, Bid Award #9686). Per an August 16, 2010 memorandum from Frank E. Lams to Mark S. Rajter, bids were opened July 29, 2010 for Athens, Troy High and the International Academy East; 15 potential bidders were solicited with 15 responding, two "No Bid" and one submitted late. Results were reviewed with Ms. Jennifer Gottlieb, Science Coordinator, and Dr. Audra Melton, Principal at International Academy East. Awards by vendor (General Fund / Capital Projects Fund / Total): Pasco Scientific $9,236.34 / $9,236.34; Science Kit $115.18 / $924.52 / $1,039.70; Sargent Welch $179.59 / $17,698.45 / $17,878.04; EAI Education $339.94 / $4,498.58 / $4,838.52; Vernier Software $6,178.60 / $6,178.60; Ward's Natural Science $51.00 / $462.00 / $513.00; Fisher Science Education $112.77 / $112.77; Carolina Biological $320.22 / $249.96 / $570.18; NASCO $15.35 / $15.35; Forestry Suppliers $190.74 / $415.74 / $606.48; Library Video Co. $89.80 / $89.80. Totals were $1,301.82 General Fund, $39,776.96 Capital Projects Fund, and $41,078.78 overall, charged to the 2010-2011 General Fund and the 2004 Capital Projects Fund. By site the totals were International Academy East $339.94 General Fund, $28,626.13 Capital Projects, $28,966.07 total; Athens High School $139.97, $5,307.51, $5,447.48; and Troy High School $821.91, $5,843.32, $6,665.23. Bid tabulations also covered Frey Scientific and Cynmar Corp.; Flinn Scientific arrived late and Arbor Scientific and Pitsco Education submitted no bid. Items priced included blood pressure sensors, EKG sensors, spirometers, colorimeters, LabQuest units, accelerometers and a SpectroVis spectrophotometer.

APPLE iPADS (Item 8.D). Scott Bryan, Technology Director, developed a process to test the viability of Apple iPads in the classroom; the equipment is available through the statewide REMC bid and the award was recommended to Apple, Inc. in the amount of $24,158.47 as an expenditure of the 2004 Capital Projects Fund. Bryan's August 27, 2010 memorandum to Frank Lams, sent from the Technology Resource Center at 4420 Livernois, Troy, Michigan 48098 (phone 248-823-5090, fax 248-823-5050), describes purchasing 44 total devices: 30 for a rotating classroom set, one each for the Directors of Technology and Instruction, one for technical evaluation, two for administrator evaluation and 9 floating checkout devices, funded as an advance purchase from the bond allocation for laptop replacement per discussions with Mr. Rajter and Dr. Fowler. Apple offers a $20 per unit discount on ten-packs from REMC Contract number 155575. Apple Inc. Education Price Quote W70740767, dated 26-AUG-2010 and valid until 25-SEP-2010, from Jason Lewandowski at 1 Infinite Loop MS: 111-HOM, Cupertino, CA 95014, lists 4 BF822LL/A iPad Wi-Fi 16GB 10-Packs at $4,790.00 each for $19,160.00; 4 MC349LL/A iPad Wi-Fi + 3G 16GB at $629.00 for $2,516.00; 4 S3788LL/A AppleCare Protection Plans at $99.00 for $396.00; 44 MC361ZM/B iPad Cases at a list of $39.00 and discounted $37.83 for $1,664.52; 10 MC552ZM/A iPad Dock Connector to VGA Adapters at $29.00 list, $28.13 discounted, for $281.30; and 5 MC531ZM/A iPad Camera Connection Kits for $140.65. The Edu List Price Total is $24,223.00, total discount $64.53, extended discounted subtotal $24,158.47, eWaste/Recycling Fee $0.00, and extended discounted total price $24,158.47 (SEA # 456352).

CLOSED SESSION (Item 11.A). A resolution was presented for the Board to go into closed session to discuss negotiations as permitted by the Michigan Open Meetings Act, Public Act 267, Section 8(c), by roll call vote of Underwood, Edmunds, Fleming, Hauff, Miletti, Philippart and Pochodylo, after which no additional business would take place other than adjournment.
